Not much, I have been part of OYO for last 6-7 year now, and what initially seemed like an exciting opportunity has turned into a deeply disappointing and exhausting experience. The company work culture is extremely toxic, with absolutely no boundaries between personal and professional life. 
There is no proper process in place and business ethics seem to be completely missing from the company's values. Employees are treated more like machines than human beings - expected to work all seven days of the week with no regards for rest, mental health, or personal time. This has been the norm for over a year now.
reviews.cons:
The more concerning is the top-down pressure from leadership. The founder frequently calls team leaders at any hour - day or night - demanding updates, creating a culture of fear and urgency that trickles down to every level of the organization. There is no concept of work-life balance, and the constant pressure is leading to burnout and widespread dissatisfaction among employees.
Many employees are staying only out of financial necessity, white actively seeking better opportunities.

If you're thinking of working at OYO, think twice. Every Saturday, we were expected to spend ₹4K–₹5K out of our own pocket just on bookings/creations — that's at least ₹20K/month, 
If your salary is ₹50K with 80% fixed and 20% variable, you're left with ₹40K. Now subtract ₹20K spent monthly on bookings and another ₹5K for team outings — you’re technically earning just ₹15K. Don’t fool yourself working 7 days a week for ₹15K. It’s exploitation, not employment.
We worked 7 days a week, and Saturdays were the worst — the manager would keep the team till 11 PM, no matter what. There's no personal space, no time for learning, no career growth, and honestly, no respect for your mental health or time.
Despite the endless work hours, the financial compensation was nowhere near fair. Add to that constant pressure, unrealistic expectations, and a manipulative work environment — it's a recipe for burnout.
This place doesn’t care about people. Just numbers. Worst experience ever.

The company lacks basic ethics in business, there are so many hidden charges that are levied upon the property owners and the reconciliation system is hard to understand (Even for someone who spent more than 3 yr working for the same role).
lets talk about the unethical business practices of Oyo - 
- The take rate of Oyo is 34 % (Which is almost 30% higher than competitors) also apart from that they will be charging additional 12% if the owner does not have GST which sums up to 46 % 
(This seems unethical but not sure ) 
- For each Booking they charge Rs. 40 from the owner's pocket for insurance which is around 4-5%, So the total taken by Oyo till date is around 50% 
- Also there are 5 different penalties that are charged to the owners i.e 
1 - Check in Deny penalty - for example a booking was received for rs 1500 and the hotel owner denies to provide check in and once Oyo finds this out they will be charging the entire 1500 rs as a penalty.  Also there's a catch here - Even if the owner requests to mark his property on soldout and does not want to be listed on Oyo still the the property will be made live without any acknowledgement from the owner by backend team and the penalty will be applied on the owner. (Lets consider this penalty amount is 4 %) 
2 - Digital Audit Penalty - If any hotelier tries to hide Oyo's booking and does not show the checkin on the app then this penalty is applied. penalty amount is 2x the commission amount. Here is the catch - The algorithm is location based but 50% of the times they aren't accurate and there is no way to reverse the penalty amount. Also even if a customer just looks for the particular property on Oyo but does not create a booking but goes to the property still Oyo will create a booking on his name and charge the hotel owner 2x penalty of commission amount. 
(Consider 4% P.m)
